newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: POLL-Argentine Peronists head B.A. province survey.
newsitem.headline: POLL-Argentine Peronists head B.A. province survey.

text.p: Argentina's ruling Peronist Party continues to lead opinion polls ahead of October midterm elections in the Buenos Aires province, the country's largest electoral district, surveys showed Monday.

In separate polls released today by Mori Argentina and CEOP, leading Argentinean polling agencies, published by El Cronista newspaper, Peronist candidate Hilda "Chiche" Duhalde, the wife of Buenos Aires Governor and presidential hopeful Eduardo Duhalde, led with 31 and 35.2 percent support, respectively, against 28 and 29.5 percent for Graciela Fernandez Meijide of the leftist coalition Frepaso.
The province's Radical Party candidate, former President Raul Alfonsin, came in third with 16.1 and 18 percent support, respectively.

In Buenos Aires city, the country's capital district, Carlos "Chacho" Alvarez of Frepaso garnered 28.2 percent of voting intentions, according to Rovier y Asociados, while in a Mora y Araujo poll he clinched 30 percent.
Alvarez is followed by Rodolfo Terragno of the Radical Party with 20.8 percent support and 21 percent support, according to each pollster.

Former Economy Minister Domingo Cavallo, also running for deputy in the capital, came in third according to the Rouvier survey with 13 percent while Peronist candidate Daniel Scioli trailed in fourth place with 11.5 percent.
Mora y Araujo, however, gave Scioli 13 percent and Cavallo only eight percent.
